column1: # the virtual gamepad starts in the 3D layout (D-pad, right stick, L3 / R3): the right stick turns the camera
# The NPDM declares 24 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true and the game's memory lives in the alias region (as Engage's, see 0100A6301214E000/game.tsv).
# The game also calls SetHeapSize(0x86000000) in nninitStartup (2.1 GB of the pool as its heap; a 2 GB heap region aborts there with 0xd401).
# What it can map is bounded by the pool less the heap (1.1 GB). The sdk build's node area is cut from ~1 GB to 62 MB (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py): measured on the Mac, the alias region is then used

# up to +1.75 GB on the Great Sky Island with 1.0 GB mapped. Without the cut it reached +2.25 GB at the first descent and the game took a memory shortage (MSF, a Blood Moon that puts Link back, issue #70).

# So 5 GB, the total proven on a phone (one reservation of at most 6 GB without the extended virtual addressing entitlement): 256 MB in front + 2.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 2.125 GB heap region
# Streamed textures are written by the CPU straight into pool memory (already in GPU layout) and published with nvnMemoryPoolFlushMappedRange (hle_nvn.c ft_add)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the host decides each frame's step in whole vsyncs and holds the frame that long (rewriter stubs at FPSLocker's sites, patches.py FRAME_STEP);
# 30 when 60 does not hold, game time = real time. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) saves power, 0 = the game's own step. Until the host has decided a step
# (the first frames) the stub steps by the measured frame time
